text: Briefing filed for BYU contained errors and citations that appeared to be AI-hallucinated. At a show-cause hearing the drafting attorney stated that he relied on several AI models in drafting the briefing, naming ClearBrief, Claude, ChatGPT and Gemini. Before the show-cause order issued he had filed a notice of errata identifying and correcting twelve errors, and counsel had voluntarily refunded opposing counsel’s fees. The court found a Rule 11(b) violation as to both attorneys on their own admissions.
asserted_by: asserting party not identified in the indexed source fields
ai_system_name: ClearBrief, Claude, ChatGPT and Gemini (named; admitted)
deployer: Chad Pehrson (drafting attorney) and Robert S. Clark (signing attorney), counsel for Brigham Young University
canonical_source_conflicted: The holdings of cited authority, including Oxford Health Plans, which counsel cited for a proposition about evident partiality under 9 U.S.C. section 10(a)(2) that the case does not address
mitigation_gap: Four separate AI tools were used in drafting and none of them, nor the signing attorney’s review, caught the fabricated and misattributed authority. The order draws no distinction between ClearBrief, a citation-checking product, and the three general-purpose models, and attributes all four to drafting rather than verification.
reliance_or_harm: The court ordered the drafting attorney to complete two CLE courses on the ethical use of AI within six months, and ordered penalties paid to the court of $2,000 from Mr Pehrson and $1,000 from Mr Clark, with proof of payment within thirty days. The refund of opposing counsel’s fees was voluntary and preceded the order, so it is not a fee-shifting sanction.
source_locator: Beus Gilbert PLLC v. Brigham Young University, No. 2:12-cv-00970-TS (D. Utah), Dkt. 385
source_review_unresolved: Professional-discipline outcomes referred to a bar or disciplinary authority are not resolved by this order and were not followed up.
No date is established for the underlying filing that carried the defective citations, so no incident date is recorded.
